record.original_question: Can the mating construction for two monic polynomials of the same degree be realized by quasiconformal surgery?

evidence.quote: The first such kind of topological surgery is mating of two monic polynomials with the same degree.
Question 2. Can matings be constructed with quasiconformal surgery?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f$ and $g$ be two monic complex polynomials of the same degree $d \geq 2$, each acting on the Riemann sphere $\widehat{\mathbb{C}}$. The formal (topological) mating of $f$ and $g$ is defined as follows. Compactify the dynamical plane of $f$ by attaching the circle at infinity $S^1_f = \{\infty \cdot e^{2\pi i\theta} : \theta \in \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}\}$, on which $f$ acts as $\theta \mapsto d\theta$, and do the same for $g$. Glue the two compactified planes along their circles at infinity by identifying the point at angle $\theta$ on $S^1_f$ with the point at angle $-\theta$ on $S^1_g$, obtaining a topological 2-sphere $\Sigma$ carrying a continuous self-map $f \sqcup_\partial g : \Sigma \to \Sigma$ of degree $d$.

One says that $f$ and $g$ are mateable, and that the geometric mating exists, if there exists a rational map $R : \widehat{\mathbb{C}} \to \widehat{\mathbb{C}}$ of degree $d$ and a semiconjugacy $\Phi : \Sigma \to \widehat{\mathbb{C}}$ from $f \sqcup_\partial g$ to $R$ that is conformal on the interiors of the filled-in dynamical planes.

Question: For every pair of monic polynomials $f, g$ of the same degree $d \geq 2$ for which the geometric mating exists, can the rational map $R$ realizing the mating be constructed by a quasiconformal surgery procedure (i.e., by cutting and pasting the dynamics of $f$ and $g$ along suitable curves and applying the measurable Riemann mapping theorem to a quasiregular model with a forward-invariant bounded-dilatation Beltrami coefficient)?
artifact.status_search_result: Quasiconformal surgery has been used successfully to construct matings in many specific settings—most notably Shishikura's surgery for postcritically finite hyperbolic polynomials, and various extensions to higher-degree and primitive tuning cases. However, a fully general quasiconformal-surgery construction of mating for all mateable pairs of monic polynomials of equal degree is not established; the surgery approach is known to apply broadly but not universally.

status_evidence.title: Quasiconformal Surgery in Holomorphic Dynamics (Branner–Fagella)
status_evidence.snippet: Since its introduction in the early 1980s quasiconformal surgery has become a major tool in the development of the theory of holomorphic dynamics.
status_evidence.claim: Quasiconformal surgery is a standard technique used to construct holomorphic maps, including matings, in many cases.

status_evidence.title: Primitive tuning via quasiconformal surgery
status_evidence.snippet: any primitive, postcritically-finite hyperbolic polynomial can be tuned with an arbitrary generalized polynomial...generalizing a result of Douady-Hubbard
status_evidence.claim: Quasiconformal surgery constructions for combining polynomials are known in many but not all cases.
